Name: Premium Squeeze Cascade
Pathway: Costs rise > wages → Affordability pressure → Reduce coverage OR lapse → Uninsured exposure grows → Event triggers crisis → Debt cascade
Mechanism: Insurance is non-discretionary. Rising costs can't be avoided—absorbed or coverage reduced. Coverage reduction creates hidden fragility.
Feedback Loops: Premium increases drive lapses; lapses increase risk pool adverse selection; adverse selection drives premium increases
Breakpoint: Premium increase forces coverage reduction or lapse

Name: Homeowners Availability Cascade
Pathway: Climate losses → Carrier exits → Non-renewals → Residual market OR uninsured → Force-placed coverage → Housing payment stress → Default risk
Mechanism: Climate risk repricing faster than expected. Private withdrawal forces expensive alternatives or uninsured exposure.
Feedback Loops: Residual market growth increases state exposure; potential assessments
Breakpoint: Consumer cannot obtain/afford coverage; lender force-places

Name: Medical Debt Cascade
Pathway: Health costs > coverage → High deductibles → Medical event → OOP exceeds ability → Medical debt → Collections → Credit damage → Bankruptcy risk
Mechanism: HDHPs shifted cost to consumers. Medical debt is unexpected, not chosen, catastrophic. Leading cause of bankruptcy.
Feedback Loops: Medical debt reduces credit access; reduced credit increases medical debt risk
Breakpoint: Medical event exceeds household ability to pay

Name: Gig Worker Insurance Trap
Pathway: Vehicle essential → Auto insurance mandatory + elevated → Premium squeeze → Pay premium OR other bills → Lapse = can't work → Continue uninsured = catastrophic exposure
Mechanism: Gig workers face double bind: vehicle essential, insurance elevated. Premium increases hit harder. Insurance is inescapable cost.
Feedback Loops: Lapse ends income; continued work without coverage concentrates risk
Breakpoint: Premium exceeds affordable share of gig income

Name: Polly-to-CARL Transmission
Pathway: Insurance stress (POLLY vectors) → Premium squeeze (less discretionary) OR coverage reduction (hidden fragility) → Insured event → Catastrophic cost → Debt cascade → CARL vectors deteriorate
Mechanism: Two channels: Direct (premium reduces income) and Latent (coverage gaps create catastrophic exposure). Latent harder to see but higher impact.
Feedback Loops: CARL stress increases insurance claims; claims increase premiums
